verdicts.trueWording: These notes are in the possession of Genly Ai
verdicts.note: vector-bsfa.com fetched live (HTTP 200, browser UA). Byline reads 'Reviewed by Nick Hubble', BSFA Review, 24 Dec 2020. Quote is verbatim in the paragraph immediately after the block quote, which also names the notes as those of Ong Tot Oppong and calls Genly Ai an ambassador from the Ekumen (page word is 'ambassador', not 'envoy'); the custody statement is explicit on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: about a fifth of the number of pages, presents cultural lore
verdicts.note: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Always_Coming_Home fetched live. Quote verbatim in the 'Summary' section, in the sentence beginning with the title of 'The Back of the Book'. Both limbs (proportion of pages, cultural lore) are on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: attributions or annotations that an ethnographic fieldworker might make
verdicts.note: Same 'Summary' sentence as index 745, continuing 'with the format and ...'. Verbatim; the ethnographic-fieldworker limb is stated, not inferred.

verdicts.trueWording: As told by Little Bear Woman of Sinshan to the Editor
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim in the 'Summary' list of items Pandora attributes to Little Bear Woman, but it is the only entry of the five with the full provenance line. The three poems are credited only 'By Little Bear Woman' with a page number and no town and no recipient; the map entry names the giver and the Editor but not a teller. The universal 'Each attributed Kesh text' is therefore not supported.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that EVERY attributed Kesh text carries teller + town + recipient

verdicts.trueWording: given to the Editor by Little Bear Woman of Sinshan
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the 'Summary' list entry for the Kesh map of the watershed of Sinshan Creek. The caption-names-the-giver limb is explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: There are not too many of them
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the page in the setting discussion of Kesh population size, introduced as Pandora observing the key difference from the reader's society, with a footnote citation. Counted: seven words, no numeral.

verdicts.trueWording: could just as easily be written in straight-forward, declarative sentences
verdicts.note: sites.middlebury.edu fetched live. Quote sits inside the comment signed 'Tori Koontz October 9, 2019 at 11:42 pm' (verified by segmenting the seven comments); the same comment names the chapter as structured in the form of field notes and continues 'Instead we see ... a slew of narrative devices', which carries the 'but is not' limb. The post is Michael Newbury's Science Fiction course blog and Koontz's comment refers to class the next day, supporting 'student reader'.

verdicts.trueWording: individual level, to the pairing level/interpersonal level, to the social
verdicts.note: Quote is verbatim and sits inside the comment signed 'Cole Easton October 9, 2019 at 10:13 pm' (verified by comment segmentation), which opens on 'The Question of Sex', the field-notes chapter. The page continues '... to the social level, to the history-shaping level'; the claim's three named levels are all present, it simply stops short of the fourth.

verdicts.trueWording: covers topics such as history, language, royal dynasties, and dragons
verdicts.note: bookreporter.com fetched live. Quote verbatim in the paragraph naming the appendix 'A Description of Earthsea'; page is signed 'Reviewed by Kathy Weissman on May 4, 2001'. All four topics are the page's own list.

verdicts.trueWording: is a compendium of reports on the society of a world
verdicts.note: ursulakleguin.com foreword page fetched live with a browser user agent (HTTP 200, 124KB) despite the site's robots.txt bar on named agents. Quote verbatim in the paragraph on 'The Matter of Seggri', which continues 'called Seggri written by various observers over a period of many years'.

verdicts.trueWording: These documents are from the archives of the Historians of Hain
verdicts.note: Verbatim, the sentence immediately following the index-757 sentence in the same 'Matter of Seggri' paragraph.

verdicts.trueWording: the first voice is that of a Mobile of the Ekumen
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the paragraph on the 1969 novel The Left Hand of Darkness, which continues 'a traveller, making a report back to the Stabiles, who stay put on Hain' and then names Genly Ai. The report limb is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: a non-directive, information-gathering consortium of worlds
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the paragraph that starts from the League of Worlds of the first three sf novels and says it morphs into the Ekumen. The definition is six words as claimed, counting each hyphenated compound as one.

verdicts.trueWording: know that it keeps happening and will happen again
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the paragraph about asking the Hainish, whose historians know a lot of what happened; the page then likens them to Ecclesiastes. Locator note: this falls a paragraph or two later than the claim's 'second paragraph', but the wording is exact and the Hainish-historians limb is explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: of Inanan Farmhold of Tag Village on the Southwest Watershed
verdicts.note: ursulakleguin.com excerpt page fetched live with a browser user agent (HTTP 200, 132KB). Quote verbatim in the byline under the heading 'Unchosen Love / Introduction', signed 'By Heokad'd Arhe of ...' and running on '... of the Budran River on Okets on the Planet O.', so the chain from farmhold to planet is complete on the page.
